experiment: Flammability and spread of cabin solids (PMMA, cotton, Nomex, foams) at 28-32 % O2, 0.6-0.8 atm, 0-20 cm/s air
why: No PSI solid-fuel burn above 22 % O2; only 5 burns lie near the habitat atmosphere (Saffire V-VI, NASA literature). Models cannot score cotton, Nomex or silicone.

experiment: Smoke-detector response to smoke made at 30 % O2 and 0.69 atm
why: SAME, SAME-R and SPICE: 86 smoke tests and 469 soot-point settings, all at 21 % O2 and 1 atm.

experiment: Still-air self-extinction of gas and emulated-solid flames at 24-33 % O2
why: ACME CFI-G has no tests between 24 % and 33 % O2, exactly where the habitat sits; burn time rises about 4.6x from Earth air to habitat air.

experiment: Release per-test FLEX-2 results (multicomponent droplets, 0.5-3 atm, up to 40 % O2)
why: FLEX-2 covers the habitat atmosphere on paper, but only its condition ranges are published in PSI.

experiment: Repeat key fabric and plastic burns at lunar (0.16 g) and Martian (0.38 g) gravity
why: No PSI combustion investigation has burned anything at partial gravity, so Moon and Mars surface decisions rest on microgravity and Earth tests alone.
